children: Qualcomm (QCOM), the wireless and computing-chip designer, gave Amazon an equity-linked reason to deepen their AI-infrastructure partnership, Reuters reported September 8. Qualcomm shares gained approximately 2.1% to $188.64 Thursday, based on the latest price shown. At that level, the stock sits 7.37% above its $175.69 GF Value, suggesting investors are already paying a modest premium for the company's expanding AI opportunity.

The headline number is hard to ignore. Amazon could eventually purchase as much as $60 billion of Qualcomm data-center products, while purchase-linked warrants could give Amazon roughly $4 billion of Qualcomm shares at $161.26 each. The companies are also working together on custom AI inference silicon and optical connectivity capable of reaching 1.6 terabits per second. That pushes Qualcomm further beyond smartphones and straight into the infrastructure spending race now reshaping the semiconductor industry.

The warrant value represents roughly 6.7% of the maximum purchasing framework, directly tying Amazon's buying activity to Qualcomm's equity story. But the missing pieces still matter: there is no disclosed minimum purchase commitment, delivery timetable or margin profile. The market is clearly assigning value to Qualcomm's cloud push, but the 7.37% premium to GF Value raises the bar. The real test now is whether this enormous potential purchasing framework converts into meaningful revenue rather than remaining an impressive headline number.

title: Qualcomm Gains 2% as Amazon's Warrant Prices AI Commitment
